strings: No permissions are set for the workflow or any of its jobs, so the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default, which may allow writes.
This actions/checkout step keeps the GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for every later step because persist-credentials is not set to false.
Action actions/checkout@v4 is not pinned to a full commit SHA, so the code behind that ref can still change.
Action actions/setup-go@v5 is not pinned to a full commit SHA, so the code behind that ref can still change.
Flags AWS access key IDs (AKIA or ASIA followed by 16 base32 characters); lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags a 40-character base64 value assigned to an AWS secret access key name; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags GitHub personal access, OAuth, user, server and refresh tokens (ghp_, gho_, ghu_, ghs_, ghr_, github_pat_); lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags GitLab personal access tokens (glpat- followed by at least 20 characters); lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags Slack bot, user, app, refresh and legacy tokens (xoxb-, xoxp-, xoxa-, xoxr-, xoxs-); lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags Slack incoming webhook, workflow and trigger URLs on hooks.slack.com; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags Stripe live secret and restricted keys (sk_live_, rk_live_); test and publishable keys are ignored; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags Google API keys (AIza followed by 35 characters), often meant for clients but still worth restricting; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags npm access tokens (npm_ followed by 36 characters); lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags PEM, OpenSSH and PGP private key blocks that have a base64 body and a footer; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.
Flags JSON Web Tokens whose first segment decodes to a JSON header with an alg field; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.

Flags a quoted high-entropy literal of 16 or more characters assigned to a password, secret, token or API key name, ignoring placeholders such as example, dummy, changeme, xxx, ${...} and process.env; lines containing repometry-ignore-secret are skipped.

Flags files that usually hold credentials: .env and .env.* except .env.example, .env.sample and .env.template, *.pem and *.key unless they hold only public certificates or keys, *.p12, *.pfx, id_rsa, id_dsa, id_ecdsa, id_ed25519, .git-credentials, and .npmrc or .pypirc with a literal auth token; repometry-ignore-secret on the first line skips the file.
eval() or the Function constructor runs a string that is not a literal, so injected text becomes code.
child_process exec or execSync runs a shell command built from interpolated or concatenated values.
The vm module compiles or runs code that is not a literal, and vm is not a security boundary.
Markup that is not a literal is written through innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML or document.write.
TLS certificate verification is turned off with rejectUnauthorized or NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED.
createHash or createHmac uses the broken MD5 or SHA-1 algorithm.
Math.random() feeds a value named like a token, secret, password, nonce, salt, key or one-time code.
A string literal points at a plain http:// URL on a public host.
A third-party action or reusable workflow is referenced by a tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.
An action owned by actions or github is referenced by a tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA.
A run script expands attacker-controlled context, such as an issue title or a branch name, directly into the shell.
A pull_request_target or workflow_run workflow checks out untrusted pull request code in a privileged job.
The workflow or one of its jobs grants the GITHUB_TOKEN write-all permissions.
Neither the workflow nor any of its jobs declares permissions, so the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository default.
An actions/checkout step leaves the GITHUB_TOKEN in the git config because persist-credentials is not false.
A reusable workflow call passes every repository secret with secrets: inherit.
A package.json dependency is installed from a URL, git repository or tarball instead of a registry version.
A package.json dependency accepts any version through "*", "latest" or an empty range.
A package.json declares a preinstall, install or postinstall script that runs whenever the package is installed.
A lockfile resolves a package over unencrypted HTTP or git transport.
A lockfile resolves a package from a host other than the public npm or Yarn registry.
A package-lock entry resolved from a registry has no integrity hash.
A FROM image has no tag or uses latest and is not pinned by digest, so rebuilds can silently change the base.
The final stage sets no USER or switches back to root, so the container runs as root.
ADD downloads a remote URL without checksum verification instead of curl with a checksum or COPY.
A RUN step pipes a curl or wget download straight into a shell, executing unverified remote code.
An ENV or ARG with a secret-looking name carries a literal value that is stored in the image or its history.
A RUN step runs apt-get upgrade or dist-upgrade, so the image contents depend on the day it was built.
A RUN step uses sudo, which is unnecessary during builds and behaves unpredictably in containers.
